Subject: Follow-up: Observability & operational tooling - next steps / POC

Hi Tom / Sarah,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the openness on your evaluation criteria. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap:
- Key priorities: per-request observability (request-level traces + correlation ids), per-route/model dashboards with p50/p95 latency, cost by token / model, retention and sampling policies, and simple alerting for latency regressions.
- You're comparing Redwood against the hyperscaler APIs (they mentioned Bedrock/Vertex) primarily for operational visibility and predictable unit economics.
- Security/compliance gate: SOC 2 evidence, data retention controls, and audit logs.

Suggested next steps / POC plan:
1) Technical deep-dive (60m) with Monica (SE) + Dev to go through observability instrumentation and the dashboards.
2) Side-by-side POC: we run a short harness to compare p50/p95 latency and token cost at target concurrency, and show per-request traces across both systems.
3) Deliverables: a short runbook with tests, a comparison sheet with measurements, and an example dashboard you can embed/query.

I attached a one-pager on Redwood observability and a draft runbook to get started. Can we lock a time next week (Tue/Wed) for the technical deep-dive? If you share the dataset/sample traffic characteristics we'll tailor the tests.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Observability & operational tooling - next steps / POC

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few additions and priorities from our side: 

Priority tests for the POC (order of importance):
1) Latency under production-like concurrency (we're typically at ~120 concurrent users producing requests with variable token lengths). Need p50/p95 and good tail behavior.
2) End-to-end traces tied to request ids — we need spans that correlate external request <> model invocation <> downstream DB/transform calls.
3) Per-model/per-route dashboards showing token counts, cost estimates, and rate limiting behavior.
4) Cost model: sample pricing (hosted vs reserved capacity) and an estimate for 100M tokens / month.
5) Compliance evidence: SOC 2 report and data retention controls.

We're also benchmarking against Bedrock and Vertex — main gap so far on their side is good request-level tracing and straightforward cost breakdowns by route (we've had to stitch logs together).

Tue/ Wed next week works. Can you include a short plan of what Redwood will run vs what Acme will run? Also cc'd Sarah who will own the logistics on our side.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director of ML Engineering, Acme Health
Tom.Reynolds@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: (internal only)
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Prep notes for Acme deep-dive (Tue 3/2)

Internal — quick prep before the call with Acme (do not forward outside the company):

Goal: Demonstrate Redwood's operational tooling advantages vs hyperscalers: instant per-request traces, simple cost-by-route breakdowns, and an example alerting rule that catches latency regressions without impacting throughput. Show how prefix/KV caching and smart batching affect token cost.

Test checklist (we should be ready to show live or simulated):
- Dashboard: per-model p50/p95, request rate, token counts, token cost estimate (demo data).
- Tracing: show a single request trace with correlation id that ties to our model invocation and to a downstream transform (use our sample pipeline).
- Load: simulate 120 concurrent users for 10 minutes at sample token distributions (short/medium/long). Capture tail latency.
- Cost: run with and without cache+batching to show delta in token consumption / cost.
- Export: demonstrate how audit logs can be exported to GCS/S3 and how retention can be configured.

Materials to bring: short slides (2-3) + the runbook and the comparison spreadsheet. Sean, please be ready to give a 5-7 minute pricing overview (hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved capacity). Dev, please have a short list of required config and any limitations for their environment. Monica, lead the instrumentation demo.

Thanks — Marissa

Tom / Sarah — thanks for the productive deep-dive today. Quick recap and concrete next steps: 

What we demonstrated:
- Live dashboard: per-model and per-route p50/p95, token usage, and a cost estimate by route.
- Tracing: full request-level traces with correlation ids and span breakdown.
- Load test: 120 concurrent users sample run (attached short report) showing p50/p95 and tail behavior.
- Cost delta: demo comparing cache+batching enabled vs disabled showing ~28% token savings on the sample workload.

Agreed next actions:
1) Redwood to provide a short POC report (measurements + screenshots) and an updated comparison spreadsheet by EOD Friday.
2) Acme to provide an anonymized 48-hour production trace if you want us to run the POC against your real distribution (we can sign an NDA/limited scoping).
3) Redwood to provide reserved capacity pricing for the volumes we discussed (Sean will follow up).

I uploaded the runbook and results to the shared drive and linked the HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-001.

Let me know if you want a follow-up meeting to review the written results.
